title: Rich text
lead: A link inside a translated sentence is the classic i18n headache: split the string into three keys and the translator loses word order. MF2 has markup for exactly this, and the Rich component renders it through snippets — the markup name in the message decides which snippet wraps the text.
demo_text: The link and its target both live in the translation, not in the component:
cta: Read {#link to=|/setup|}the docs{/link} before you ship
options_text: A snippet receives a snippet for the markup's contents and the markup's MF2 options — \{#link to=|/x|\} becomes \{ to: '/x' \} — so a translation can carry per-locale attributes. They are input like any other, so check them before they reach an attribute: the snippets on this page only let a path on this site through. Nesting works to any depth; each level goes through its own snippet:
fallback_title: Missing snippets don't break the page
fallback_text: Markup with no matching snippet still renders its contents — so an outdated translation, or one written before a snippet existed, degrades gracefully instead of vanishing:
unwired: This sentence has {#glow}unwired markup{/glow} in the middle
parts_text: formatParts(key, params) is the primitive underneath — it returns text / open / close / standalone parts. Reach for it directly if you'd rather render markup with machinery of your own.
names_text: Markup names become snippet names, so keep them valid identifiers — \{#my-link\} has no writable snippet.
